tip: The 'nos' is what makes it mutual: 'echamos de menos' alone means we miss (someone). Add 'nos' and the missing points both ways – we miss each other.
Not 'for the morning' – with parts of the day, 'por' just means 'in'. 'Vengo por la mañana' = I come in the morning: a loose timeframe, nothing traded.
'Te lo explico': indirect pronoun ('te') comes first, then direct ('lo'), then the verb.
'Ir' = go, 'irse' = leave. The 'nos' in 'Nos vamos' isn't 'us' – it flips go into depart: we're off at eight, destination irrelevant.
'Firme' isn't a typo for 'firma' – that final '-e' is the 'usted' command. Formal orders swap the vowel: 'firme', 'pase', 'disculpe'. The '-a' form would sound chummy.
You don't 'go through the wrong door' – you mistake yourself OF door: 'se equivocó de puerta'. 'Equivocarse de' + bare noun, no article, for any wrong-X.
'Quedarse' = to stay/remain. Different from 'quedar' (to arrange to meet). 'Me quedé en casa' = I stayed home.
'Se me olvidó': accidental 'se' construction – 'it slipped my mind'.
Because 'dije' is past, the subjunctive time-travels with it: 'viniera', not 'venga'. Spanish matches the order's tense to when you gave it.
Telling someone NOT to do it changes the verb: '¡abre!' = open!, but 'No abras' = don't open. Negative 'tú' commands borrow the subjunctive form.
'Olvidársele' – unplanned event: 'se nos olvidó' – we forgot (accidentally).
Why 'los zapatos', not 'sus zapatos'? The 'se quita' already says whose they are – Spanish drops 'her' with clothes and body parts.
'Por' = in exchange for: 'Lo compré por diez euros.' 'Por' for what you pay or trade.
Why 'se la envié', never 'le la'? Two l-pronouns can't touch: 'le' turns into 'se' before 'lo/la'. The 'se' here is the director, not a reflexive.
'Suele' is from 'soler': 'soler' + infinitive = to usually do something (habitual).
'Desde los cuatro años' + plain present = 'has dressed herself since four'. Spanish uses now-tense for still-true situations – no 'has been' machinery.
Her eyes act on their own: 'le lloran los ojos' = 'the eyes cry to her'. Spanish hands the person a 'le' and lets the body part be the subject.
'En que' = in which/on which: 'El día en que llegó' = The day on which he arrived. Preposition + 'que' for things.
'Costar' prices effort, not just money: 'Le cuesta levantarse' = getting up 'costs him'. The struggler is 'le', the struggle is the subject – a 'gustar'-style flip.
'Para' = for (recipient): 'Es para ti.' 'Para' marks who receives something.
'Oler' takes 'a', not 'como', for what something smells of: 'huele a comida' is literally 'smells to food'. The 'a' marks the source of the smell.
'Tocar' means touch – Spanish speakers literally 'touch the guitar'. And it's normally 'la guitarra' with the article, not 'toca guitarra' like English 'plays guitar'.
Two l-pronouns can't touch: 'le las envié' is illegal, so 'le' morphs into 'se' – 'Se las envié'. That 'se' isn't reflexive, it's 'le' in disguise.
Deadline = 'para', never 'por': 'para el viernes' means done BY Friday. 'Por el viernes' would drift toward 'around Friday' – your boss wants 'para'.
'Me gustaría' + infinitive – polite way to express a wish.
'Por' = because of. Expresses the cause or obstacle: 'No salimos por la lluvia' (We didn't go out because of the rain).
'Quiero que' flips the next verb to subjunctive: 'sean', not 'son'. You're wishing happiness on them, not reporting it – Spanish marks that gap in the verb itself.
Don't reach for 'realizar' – that means to carry out. To notice/realize is 'darse cuenta': 'Me di cuenta del error', literally 'I gave myself account'.
'Lleva' = takes AWAY from where you are; 'trae' = brings toward you. She 'lleva a sus hijos' to school because the speaker isn't standing at the school.
'Por' = because of. Expresses what caused something: 'Lo hice por ti' (I did it because of you).
